senses.sense_definition: To destroy completely, eliminate, or eradicate something unwanted.

examples.text: The government made strong efforts to <w>extirpate</w> corruption from all public institutions.
Reformers sought to <w>extirpate</w> every remaining trace of the old oppressive regime.

senses.sense_definition: To cause a species or population to become locally extinct in a specific geographical area.

examples.text: Gray wolves were completely <w>extirpated</w> from the national park during the twentieth century.
Pollution threatens to <w>extirpate</w> rare native fish species across the entire river basin.

senses.sense_definition: To pull up by the roots; to uproot.

examples.text: The gardeners worked all morning to <w>extirpate</w> the deeply rooted invasive weeds.
Careful farmers must <w>extirpate</w> harmful plants before planting next season's crops.

senses.sense_definition: To clear land or an area of tree stumps and roots.

examples.text: Pioneers spent weeks using heavy machinery to <w>extirpate</w> the forest clearing for farming.
They decided to <w>extirpate</w> the abandoned field before starting the construction project.

senses.sense_definition: To remove an organ or diseased tissue completely by surgical excision.

examples.text: The surgeon was forced to <w>extirpate</w> the entire malignant tumor to prevent recurrence.
A specialist operated quickly to <w>extirpate</w> the damaged tissue from the patient's abdomen.

senses.sense_definition: Rooted out, extinct, or utterly destroyed.

examples.text: The ancient tribe was declared utterly <w>extirpate</w> after the devastating conflict.
He hoped the rebellious factions were fully subdued and <w>extirpate</w> throughout the kingdom.

traits.comment: Rare or obsolete adjectival form meaning eradicated.
